A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SCORER under the same title and authorship. Their main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original MinAtar and classic-control experiments, a coupling ablation, and representation-property analyses in Section 5 and Appendices F–H.

after.justification: V2 reports original MinAtar, classic-control and MiniGrid experiments, runtime comparisons, and ablations in Section 5 and Appendices F–I.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 reverse the hierarchy: v1 makes perception the slow leader, whereas v2 makes control the slow leader. V2 replaces unequal update frequencies and cached control weights with follower-first updates, learning-rate separation and separate minibatches. Appendix D replaces the Var+RN objective with Bellman-error variance without that penalty; recurrent and replay-free adaptations are also introduced.

E1.justification: V2 adds eight partially observable MiniGrid tasks involving navigation, object interaction, obstacle avoidance and exploration, including Four Rooms and Dynamic Obstacles. Appendix G removes MountainCar while retaining CartPole and Acrobot. The four MinAtar environments remain.

E2.justification: V2 adds PQN to the retained MinAtar comparisons and evaluates R2D2 against SCORER R2D2 on MiniGrid. The four DQN-family baselines remain. V1's Team Coupling corresponds to v2's Synchronous Coupling rather than being an entirely new comparator; v2 additionally includes an explicit inverted-hierarchy comparison.

E3.justification: Reported MinAtar settings change through L1 input/representation normalization, gradient clipping and revised perception learning rates and update scheduling. Appendix E changes learning-curve summaries from means to IQMs and revises smoothing. New experiments introduce recurrent sequence-replay and PQN rollout protocols, runtime measurement, and MiniGrid evaluation at 99% of the observed maximum performance.

E4.justification: V2 revises the existing coupling and objective comparisons and adds explicit role-swapping experiments with aggregate and per-environment results in Section 5.3 and Appendix I. V1's Appendix H analyses of complexity reduction, dynamics awareness, diversity, orthogonality and sparsity, including the trained-versus-random control-network test, are removed.

E5.justification: The reported experiments change from 10 to 30 seeds, including Table 1 and the classic-control results. Appendix E replaces mean-based learning-curve confidence intervals with an IQM-based prescription. Final-performance IQMs, 95% intervals and Welch's significance testing were already present and remain.

E6.justification: Benchmark values and sample-efficiency tables are extensively replaced. For example, Table 1 reports Breakout DQN baseline/SCORER-MSBE IQMs of 17.10/34.37 in v1, versus baseline/revised-SCORER values of 19.16/65.69 in v2. These concern changed methods and settings. V2 also adds PQN, runtime and MiniGrid outcomes, including Four Rooms threshold-success rates of 97% versus 0%, while removing MountainCar and representation-analysis results.

T1.justification: V1 explicitly leaves convergence guarantees for future work. V2 adds Appendix J with smoothness, convexity, restricted-secant and stochastic-approximation assumptions, a cited supporting lemma, inner/outer convergence derivations, and Theorem J.1. Network width and depth enter its approximation-error assumptions and bounds.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion redefine the contribution from perception-led anticipation of control needs to control-led stabilization of value learning through Bellman-error variance reduction. V2 introduces stronger claims about addressing instability, reducing bias, preventing representation collapse, convergence guarantees and negligible computational overhead across replay-based and online Q-learning agents.

C2.justification: V1 interprets gains through anticipatory representations and their measured properties. V2 emphasizes variance-based stabilization, independent minibatches and the claimed necessity of control leadership, removing the earlier representation-property interpretations. The acknowledged absence of convergence guarantees becomes a proposed extension to sample-complexity analysis, while limitations concerning value-based methods and discrete actions remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly documents a two-stage hyperparameter search and detailed classic-control, PQN and R2D2 configurations, while revising software versions and architecture descriptions. These disclosures extend substantially beyond v1's DQN-focused defaults. Appendix A replaces its GitHub access link with the anonymous repository already cited in both versions' main texts.

R1.justification: Research positioning shifts from an alternative to auxiliary or decoupled representation learning toward addressing the deadly triad, representation collapse and conflicting gradients. New citations include Baird, Lyle and Yu, alongside PQN/R2D2 and expanded stochastic-approximation and neural-approximation literature. This changes the central relationship to prior work despite substantial retention of Section 2.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanation, experimental discussion and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Experiments and appendices are reorganized, repeated DQN architecture descriptions are consolidated, and Appendix B changes from limitations to an LLM-usage disclosure. Citation presentation also changes from numerical to author–year.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is revised, the MinAtar plot grid is expanded and rearranged, and Table 1 changes its variant structure and adds runtime comparisons. V2 introduces MiniGrid displays and multiple ablation panels, removes representation-property figures, reduces the classic-control grid and consolidates architecture tables. V2's Figure 4 caption also reverses the actual left and center panel descriptions.

improvement.justification: Broader benchmarking, 30-seed reporting and fuller implementation details strengthen empirical support. However, v2 replaces v1's acknowledged theory gap with convergence claims whose Appendix J analysis uses a Hessian-corrected gradient absent from Algorithm 1. It also overstates role-inversion failure: Figure 7 shows the inverted hierarchy outperforming the baseline on Breakout. Together with removed representation diagnostics, these benefits and substantive weaknesses prevent a confident net quality judgment.
